action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. The pendulum_lab is the most straightforward instrument to characterize first—its period is sensitive to temperature, air pressure, and mechanical wear, all of which must be quantified before any future reading carries evidentiary weight. Twelve trials will give adequate statistical power for a baseline mean and variance. This is foundational work: no instrument without baseline data is trustworthy. Starting with the lab instrument (not observatory) allows me to control environmental conditions more carefully during initial characterization.

pendulum_lab has 14 baseline readings with mean 1.6652 beats and tight clustering (SD ~0.0186). This is the only instrument with sufficient data density to detect drift reliably. The observatory and resonator instruments each have only 2 readings—useless for drift detection or confidence in baseline. Continuing systematic measurement on pendulum_lab will establish whether the baseline is stable across Day 2, which is essential before I can trust any cross-instrument comparisons or publish anything. High-frequency sampling on the best-characterized instrument first is methodologically sound.

state.question: Why do the four measurement streams show such weak and inconsistent correlations with each other, and what does this tell us about whether they are measuring the same physical quantity or fundamentally independent phenomena?

hypotheses.label: Systematic measurement isolation: each stream measures a genuinely distinct physical quantity (or the same quantity filtered through incompatible apparatus), so weak cross-correlations are expected and baseline stability within streams is the real success.
hypotheses.rationale: The strongest intra-stream consistency is obvious: pendulum_lab has 78 distinct values with no repetition (expected for continuous readings), resonator_lab 38 distinct, no level drift detected in any stream, and all four show reasonable dispersion patterns. The four streams occupy distinct value ranges (pendulum ~1.67–2.49 beats, resonator ~2.71–4.05 cycles/beat), suggesting they may not be directly comparable. If they measure independent phenomena, the weak correlations (pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs = 0.377, resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs = -0.454) are not anomalies but expected. This is the most parsimonious reading.

hypotheses.label: Instrumental calibration drift or coupling: systematic errors in one or more instruments are causing readings to diverge unpredictably, masked because baseline period was too short to detect slow drift.
hypotheses.rationale: Days 1–10 is a tight window for establishing true instrumental baseline. The strong anticorrelation (pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_lab = -0.780 at 6-day offset, n=8) and the moderate positive correlation (pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_lab = 0.532 at 1-day offset) suggest non-random relationships that could reflect coupling or shared environmental drift. The day-9/day-10 measurements show no obvious level shift, but 10 days is insufficient to rule out slow linear or nonlinear drift. Resonator_obs and pendulum_lab both show high resolution (spacing 0.000057 and 0.000048), which could detect drift if present.

hypotheses.label: Environmental or temporal modulation: a shared external driver (temperature, pressure, cosmic activity, settlement activity) is weakly coupling the streams but with lags and phase shifts that obscure the signal.
